definitions.explanation: The entertainment district east of Shinjuku Station, packed with bars, restaurants, cinemas, host and hostess clubs, and neon signs. The name is used as shorthand for a loud, late-night, slightly disreputable part of town.

examples.japanese: {歌舞伎町|かぶきちょう}で{飲|の}んだ。
{歌舞伎町|かぶきちょう}の{夜|よる}はネオンで{明|あか}るい。
examples.english: Kabukicho at night is bright with neon.

examples.japanese: {終電|しゅうでん}を{逃|のが}した{人|ひと}たちが、{朝|あさ}まで{歌舞伎町|かぶきちょう}の{店|みせ}で{時間|じかん}をつぶしていた。
examples.english: People who had missed the last train were killing time in Kabukicho's bars until morning.

notes:
A neighborhood of {新宿区|しんじゅくく} in Tokyo. The name comes from a post-war plan to build a kabuki theater there; the theater was never built, but the name stuck.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {眠|ねむ}らない{街|まち}: the city that never sleeps — a standard epithet for the district
- {歌舞伎町|かぶきちょう}{一番街|いちばんがい}: the main gate-marked street at its entrance
- ホストクラブ: host club — the business the district is most associated with

CULTURAL NOTE:
In conversation the name carries connotations of nightlife and of trouble: saying someone works or hangs around {歌舞伎町|かぶきちょう} implies a world of late hours and drinking. Despite the name, it has nothing to do with kabuki as a performing art — for that, see {歌舞伎|かぶき}.
